translations.answer: The hardware layer inherits from LeggedHW and implements read() and write() functions; the model layer follows legged_unitree_description to generate xacro/URDF files and adheres to joint/link naming conventions. This allows platform differences to be consolidated at the hardware interface and model description, without affecting the NMPC/WBC core.
translations.applicability: Applicable to the ROS1/ros-control framework; the repository is no longer maintained, and modern systems should evaluate migration costs.
translations.credibility.rationale: The issue has been closed, the environment is clear and free of conflicts, and there is formal documentation or exact citation of independent reproducibility.
translations.details.attempts.0: Inherit LeggedHW and implement read()/write() functions.
translations.details.attempts.1: Imitate unitree_description to generate URDF files and maintain joint/link naming conventions.
translations.details.attempts.2: Only start real-time state estimation and legged_controller on real hardware.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Check the hardware interface, description file, controller, and state estimator against the official repository directory.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: Isolate platform differences via ros-control hardware interface; separate simulation from hardware in official startup order.
translations.details.environments.0: ROS/ros-control; OCS2; A1; author uses a 11th-gen NUC, NMPC frequency close to 200 Hz; repository currently marked as no longer maintained.
translations.details.limits.0: Repository is no longer maintained; version, dependencies, and safety boundaries must be re-verified against current fork.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Official README lists multiple lab runs on A1 and provides historical records of 2 hours to 1 day; author's structure matches the repository.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: What is the minimum compatibility boundary when migrating legged_control to a custom legged robot?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: Why can't simulation controller and real controller be mixed?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Official README explicitly states that real hardware cannot start cheater controller; initial control should use cradle, low gain, limit, and emergency stop.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Hardware read/write interface and joint naming do not meet framework assumptions.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: Using simulation truth state or simulation load on real hardware.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Direct modification of the main repository makes hardware compatibility hard to maintain.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Real hardware starting cheater controller or running Gazebo on board causes incorrect state or resource risks.
translations.media_summaries.0: The main framework diagram shows trajectory → NMPC → WBC → forward force torque + low gain PD, and IMU/actuator state → Kalman filter; the repository README text is consistent with this.
